answer.held_back_by: Plain speaking and pushing the bottom 20th three Budgets in a row cost me STAND with seniors, and a thin GE result (55.9%) didn't help. I was trusted but never quite seen as one of them, so I topped out at MR3-ish minister, short of the larger portfolio.
answer.ending_fair_why: Clean integrity, a respectable ministerial career and a legacy of people I trained is about what that pattern of choices deserves. The Declassified reveal of ceilings I never knew was a nice sting. I'd have liked the open threads (stallholder, forum letter, the man's case, who the Minister was) resolved.
answer.chase_next: The Permanent Secretary route, staying in the service rather than going into politics. The card says my ceiling was raised to that, and I want to see whether a career that rewards candour and mentoring ends there instead of in a GRC.
answer.play_again_why: Not this minute. It was a good one-life story but the late years thinned out, and I'd want a break before testing a different path.

tone_breaks.line: You served. The service continued. Both of these facts are entirely unremarkable and that is the highest compliment the system can pay.
tone_breaks.note: Funny and close to true, but it is slightly self-aware. It is fine at the ending, I'd keep it out of mid-game text.

tone_breaks.line: GE returned team at 55.9%, down from 61.2%, called 'a timely reminder'.
tone_breaks.note: Not a break, I liked it. 'Timely reminder' is exactly the phrase for a drop. Leaving it here so you keep it.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is about being confirmed in grade, how appraisals describe you and what the system quietly decides about your ceiling. Salary is only a number on the card. Minister Salary makes it sound like a satire about pay, which it isn't.
